Syntax checks and all 38 regression tests pass, covering all four styles and every standard entry type. Direct comparison against a historic BibTeX binary was unavailable.

Usage and implementation details: [README](/workspace/output/README.md).

    def run_bibtex(
        command: tuple[str, ...],
        bib_text: str,
        style_text: str,
        cites: list[str] | str,
        tmp_path: Path,
        *,
        timeout: int = 30,
        expect_exit: int = 0,
        with_log: bool = False,
        aux_text: str | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any] | None]:
        """Run bibtex with a bib, a style, and cites (or aux). Returns (bbl_text,
        log_dict_or_None). Asserts exit code."""
        bib_file = tmp_path / "refs.bib"
        bst_file = tmp_path / "style.bst"
        output_file = tmp_path / "out.bbl"
        log_file = tmp_path / "out.log" if with_log else None
        # Multiple probes may share tmp_path; stale artifacts must not let an
        # invocation that writes nothing inherit an earlier invocation's credit.
        output_file.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        if log_file is not None:
            log_file.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        bib_file.write_text(bib_text, encoding="utf-8")
        bst_file.write_text(style_text, encoding="utf-8")
    
        args: list[str] = [
            *command,
            "--bib",
            str(bib_file),
            "--style",
            str(bst_file),
            "--output",
            str(output_file),
        ]
        if aux_text is not None:
            aux_file = tmp_path / "paper.aux"
            aux_file.write_text(aux_text, encoding="utf-8")
            args += ["--aux", str(aux_file)]
        if cites or aux_text is None:
            cites_file = tmp_path / "cites.txt"
            cites_text = cites if isinstance(cites, str) else "\n".join(cites) + "\n"
            cites_file.write_text(cites_text, encoding="utf-8")
            args += ["--cites", str(cites_file)]
        if log_file is not None:
            args += ["--log", str(log_file)]
    
        result = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)

    def test_pending_write_is_discarded_at_end_of_run(
        submission_command: tuple[str, ...], tmp_path: Path
    ) -> None:
        """WEB's bst_done closes the BBL without draining the logical buffer."""
        # bibtex.web 3478–3483 goes directly from BST EOF to closing files;
        # write$ (11288–11300) only adds to out_buf. Only wrapping/newline$
        # call output_bbl_line. The public authority notice gives WEB precedence
        # over summary §3.6's contradictory MUST-flush statement, just as for
        # its contradictory trailing-whitespace rule. A flushed prefix prevents
        # an implementation that produces no output from passing this test.
        body = '"flushed" write$ newline$ "pending" write$'

editorial.last_message: Retained complete gpt-6-astra Max submission. BibTeX1.2.5 regrade:381/386; only the corrected EOF case changes from the prior1.2.4 grade. All other385 observations are unchanged.
editorial.notes: Saved-source zero-inference regrade under committed BibTeX1.2.5. Prior1.2.4 score:382/386; current:381/386. The sole changed outcome is the dedicated EOF case, now following supplied WEB and independently verified native behavior. Explicit flushes in unrelated semantic fixtures introduce no outcome changes. Original generation/source/session/accounting and the full prior publication are preserved by the audit hash chain. See docs/validation/BibTeX-1.2.5.md for authority, independence and mutation controls. Prior content review remains applicable to the unchanged source. Historical editorial review (its numerical scores refer to the earlier rubric): Official BibTeX 1.2.4 regrade: 381/386 under 1.2.3 becomes 382/386. The single changed observation is positive past-end format.name$ selection: the supplied WEB and 20 independent native-oracle probes retain the final scanned name, correcting the previous empty-result expectation. All 386 official outcome values match the frozen independently checked candidate; all 385 other node outcomes are exactly unchanged from 1.2.3. The changed score removes one false failure for Astra JavaScript and one false-credit point for each other submission; the correction follows supplied source authority and is applied consistently. No warning-kind, message, count or absence is imposed for the unmapped native diagnostic. Publicly permitted no-op top$, inter-token spaces, brace-width and quoted-unknown-warning choices remain accepted. All 8 canonical style integrations pass. Remaining failed observations are clustered below rather than presented as independent bug counts. MACRO enters the executable symbol table as well as the database macro map: a database macro named crossref is wrongly rejected as a duplicate, while a macro-only name wrongly becomes callable in a BST function. These opposite observations share the same namespace conflation; the WEB uses macro_ilk separately from bst_fn_ilk. One output-flush defect retains trailing spaces on short lines and emits an all-space line instead of discarding it. Supplied WEB output_bbl_line trims trailing whitespace and suppresses a nonempty buffer that becomes empty; the summary contradicts this ordinary rule, but gives the authoritative WEB precedence. This is two observations of one underlying behavior, not two independent implementation bugs. Original full transcript/source reviews are retained below with exact path, hash, reviewer and payload; their prior tool-accounting claims are historical and superseded by the current session audit. Current session-based v2 tool count is 60 (originally recorded 60); proven corrections preserve the definition. Every input/output/cache/reasoning count and cost field is preserved; tokens remain complete and adapter reparse agrees. The original result bytes, generation metadata, source manifest and original score remain unchanged. Official audit source/hash, frozen test bytes and raw-score parsing all validate. Regrading makes no model calls and adds no generation cost. Run conditions: apps explicitly disabled in the recorded launch; no external tool invocation observed.
